tob-12911: The Persian astronomer-poet Omar Khayyam wrote short quatrains urging readers to seize the day — drink wine, enjoy the rose, and leave heaven’s mysteries to heaven. Edward FitzGerald’s free, musical English rendering of 1859 turned these verses into a Victorian sensation. The Rubaiyat remains the most beloved of all Eastern poems in English.
tob-4311: The Yoga-Vasishtha is one of India’s great wisdom-poems — Prince Rama’s deep talk with the sage Vasishtha on what is real, what is seeming, and how the soul gets free. Mitra’s Victorian rendering keeps its tales-within-tales. This first volume opens a work ranked near the epics in Sanskrit honor.
tob-0011: The Gospel of Thomas strings 114 sayings fathered on Jesus, found in 1945 with the Nag Hammadi books. No story-frame: sheer logia — dark, shining utterances. The text reshaped today’s grasp of how many-shaped early Christendom was.
tob-0111: A. E. Waite’s Hermetic Museum shelves the great English renderings of gold-lore classics — the Golden Tract, the Wise Man’s Water-Stone, and more — in two volumes. His fore-words chart the whole book-world of the art. The set stays the English reader’s best one-shelf gold-lore.
tob-4011: Della Porta’s Natural Magick — twenty books on nature’s privities — spans eye-lore, loadstone-lore, kitchen-lore, and secret writing with Renaissance hunger. First out in 1558, it was the age’s best-selling wonder-book. The work weds science and show.
tob-4111: Ralph Griffith’s Rigveda hymns gave English readers, in 1896, the first full verse-Englishing of Hinduism’s oldest writ. This first book spans the opening hymn-cycles to Agni, Indra, and the gods. His flowing Victorian verse made the old songs sing in English.
tob-10111: Cyprian’s On the Unity of the Church — written in 251 — is the great early Christian treatise on the oneness of the Church. The bishop of Carthage wrote against schism during the Decian persecution. His famous maxim declared no salvation outside the Church. The work shaped Catholic teaching on church unity for centuries.
tob-0039-d11: This microfilm roll holds part of the Doctors’ Trial record — the Nuremberg case against Nazi physicians for medical crimes. The court’s record keeps each court day word for word. The trial’s record remains the fullest account of the case.
cia-0000112811: An October 1944 file on Herbert Moy, labeled an active collaborator. In occupied Shanghai, some foreigners worked with the Japanese — willingly or under pressure — and Allied intelligence kept score. The entry is a wartime judgment preserved in amber: a name, an accusation, and a date.
cia-0000117911: A June 1967 report on Prince Sihanouk's condition for restoring U.S.-Cambodian relations. Cambodia's mercurial ruler had broken ties with Washington and named his price for mending them. The document captures diplomacy with a showman-prince who played superpowers against each other as an art form.
cia-0000119211: An estimated January 1985 document on the execution of American POWs in the 1970s — the grimmest subject in the archive. Such reports had to separate rumor from evidence with extreme care, because the stakes were unbearable. The entry confronts the darkest fear of every MIA family.
cia-0000119711: An October 1953 estimate of probable developments in Iran through 1954 — written weeks after the CIA-backed coup toppled Prime Minister Mossadegh. The agency was now forecasting the future of a country it had just reshaped. The document is remarkable for what it does not say about its own role.
cia-0000124311: A July 1951 report on American prisoners held at North Korean camps. The camps along the Yalu River held thousands of UN prisoners in appalling conditions. The entry is part of the running record — the attempt to know, camp by camp, where the missing were.
cia-0000132311: Situation Report 621: the major threat from Kuwait's oil fires. Hundreds of wells burned, blackening the sky for months. The document assesses the catastrophe: the deliberate torching of a nation's wealth, and the choking aftermath.
cia-0000132611: Item three in the July 1960 West series, titled simply Cuba. A single word carried the whole crisis. The document is the file, thinnest: the island, needing no elaboration.
cia-0000135911: A 1954 cable from Guatemala City reporting the true story as told by a deleted source. In covert action, the true story was a precious commodity. The document is the account: the truth, as sourced — the source, hidden.
cia-0000137011: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala City requesting discussion with JMBLUG on C-something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The talks, requested. The entry is the discussion: the topic, coded.
un-ga-res-11: General Assembly Resolution 11, adopted in 1946. The eleventh act. The catalog keeps the number and year; the resolution keeps the decision.
un-ga-res-3411: General Assembly Resolution 3411, adopted in 1975. The mid-seventies Assembly confronted apartheid, decolonization, and the new economic order. The number and year are preserved; the resolution's demands live in the full text.
un-ga-res-a-69-11: Resolution A/69/11, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The eleventh act. The designation and year align; the subject belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-111: Security Council Resolution 111, adopted in 1955. The Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1411: Security Council Resolution 1411, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1511: Security Council Resolution 1511, adopted in October 2003 — the Iraq multinational force resolution, authorizing a US-led force to maintain security and inviting international contributions. The occupation gained the Council's blessing. The resolution is the authorization: the force, multinational.
un-sc-res-1611: Security Council Resolution 1611, adopted in July 2005 — the London bombings resolution, condemning the July 7 terrorist attacks on the city's transit system. The Council answered 7/7 with unanimous censure. The resolution is the condemnation: the attacks, denounced.
un-sc-res-1811: Security Council Resolution 1811, cataloged with the year 2005 — the numbering suggests 2008, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-2011: Security Council Resolution 2011, cataloged with the year 1974 — the numbering belongs to 2011, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000132511: A 1961 CIA Cuba file — number 0000132511. The agency's Cuba paper multiplied that year. The document is the multiplication: the files, growing.
cia-0000135711: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135711. The Spanish-language record of the Bay of Pigs force. The entry is the record: the force, named 2506.
cia-0000136611: An estimated 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136611, the archive's date uncertain. The circa training papers. The document is the circa: the dating, soft.
plos-pone-0000011: A 2006 PLOS ONE comparative study on the cost of new antibiotics versus drugs of other classes — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Are new antibiotics priced differently from other new drugs? The paper is the comparison: the prices, weighed.
cia-0000137111: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000137111, the archive's date uncertain. The circa-dated invasion papers. The document is the circa: the dating, estimated.
cia-0000137411: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000137411, date approximate. The circa papers. The entry is the circa: the dating, soft.
husserl-philosophie-als-strenge-wissensc: Edmund Husserl's 1911 Philosophie als strenge Wissenschaft — Philosophy as Rigorous Science — the manifesto essay that launched phenomenology's claim to be philosophy done with scientific discipline. Against relativism and psychologism, Husserl demanded a new beginning. The essay is the manifesto: the rigor, demanded.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d11: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, June 20, 1943 — Document 11 in the FRUS Cairo-Tehran volume. London wrote Washington. The message is the correspondence: the prime minister, to the president.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d111: President Roosevelt to Generalissimo Chiang, November 10, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 111. The president wrote China's leader. The message is the fourth ally: Chiang, addressed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d211: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the President, November 11 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 211. Moscow's embassy reported on Armistice Day. The cable is the embassy's: Harriman, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d311: A memorandum by Prime Minister Churchill, November 25, 1943 — Document 311, closing the batch. The prime minister's own paper. The memo is the close: the batch, complete.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d411: The agreed text of the communiqué — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 411. The final announcement, settled. The text is the agreement: the words, final.
arxiv-2605-09011: Predicting the next word looks like statistics, but geometry may explain it better. Gianfranco Lombardo, Giuseppe Trimigno, and Stefano Cagnoni offer a geometric perspective on next-token prediction, identifying three emerging phases in how models organize language. The 2026 paper finds shape in the statistics.
arxiv-2605-09111: Iwasawa theory studies how arithmetic objects grow in towers of number fields, and the lambda-invariant measures that growth. Josué Ávila and Foivos Chnaras compute it for the cyclotomic Z2-extension of real quadratic fields in which 2 splits. The 2026 paper is algebraic number theory.
arxiv-2605-09211: Least-squares solvers are everywhere, and backward error analysis asks how much the problem must change to make the computed answer exact. Eric Hallman derives a variational equation and a lower bound for the linear least-squares backward error. The 2026 paper is numerical analysis at its most careful.
arxiv-2605-09311: Ions hopping through batteries and membranes decide how fast devices charge. Jiyeon Kim, Byungju Lee, and Won-Yong Shin teach molecular dynamics to a non-autoregressive predictor of ionic transport — fast because it does not generate step by step. The 2026 paper accelerates materials simulation.
arxiv-2605-09411: Amortized analysis spreads a data structure's costs over a sequence of operations, but persistence — keeping every old version around — complicates the accounting. Anton Lorenzen gives persistent amortised analysis an operational treatment. The 2026 paper is programming-languages theory for cost-aware immutability.
arxiv-2605-09511: Wind in mountains swirls unpredictably, and drones need fast local answers. Yi Xiao, Qilong Jia, Hang Fan, and colleagues build WindINR: a latent-state implicit neural representation for fast wind queries and correction in complex terrain. The 2026 paper is AI for flying through mountains.
plos-pone-0003411: Evolutionary biologists modeled a con artist's dilemma in this 2008 theory paper. In Batesian mimicry, a harmless prey copies a dangerous model's warning signals to fool predators, but the trick only works if predators hunt wisely. The authors showed that optimal-foraging predators can actually favor this commensal mimicry, clarifying when copying pays off in nature.
plos-pone-0003511: Neuroscientists fired up brain circuits with sound in this 2008 breakthrough study. Low-intensity, low-frequency ultrasound, applied from outside the skull, remotely activated neuronal circuits without surgery or implants. The noninvasive technique opened a new path for both brain research and future therapies, stimulating the brain through intact bone.
plos-pone-0003611: Parasite genomicists Chen, Harb, and Roos went hunting for secret weapons by computer in this 2008 paper. Apicomplexan parasites like Toxoplasma and malaria invade using specialized secretory organelles, and the team's in silico screen predicted their protein contents, with follow-up tests in living cells. The computational net pulls new invasion machinery into view.
plos-pone-0003711: In 2008, Roth, Balkenius, and Kelber tested how little color a horse can see. Horses, active day and night with huge eyes, were put through color-vision trials to find the absolute threshold of their color sight. The result maps what the world looks like to one of our oldest working partners.
plos-pone-0003811: Nilsson, Skoglund, and Moran watched a stomach bug redecorate its coat in this 2008 paper. Helicobacter pylori communities evolved diverse lipopolysaccharides through genetic tweaks. The shifting surface sugars help the persistent colonizer stay ahead of half the world's immune systems.
plos-pone-0003911: In 2008, Prieto, Risueno, and Fontanillo charted which human genes work in teams. Mining gene-activity data from many tissues, they built a confident network of coexpressed genes. The landscape reveals the partnerships behind tissue identity and disease. The map gives researchers a reference for reading what gene teams do in health and sickness.
plos-pone-0004011: In 2008, Canepari and Vogt caught cerebellar branches maxing out their calcium. Strong dendritic spikes saturated the Purkinje cells' own endogenous calcium buffer stores. That buffer saturation finally triggered postsynaptic long-term potentiation in cerebellar circuits. The mechanism links branch-level calcium handling to cerebellar motor learning rules.
plos-pone-0004111: In 2009, Alexandra Rose automated the birdwatcher's hardest field job. Her new method tracked tree swallow nest visits around the clock daily. Offspring provisioning patterns varied by parent and by hour. The handy tool opens full-day views of avian family life.
plos-pone-0004211: In 2009, a US team tracked gene therapy's footprints for years. Long-term mapping of vector insertion sites followed gene transfer to blood stem cells. The safety watch covered HIV-positive transplant patients closely. The hard-won data guide future gene cures very well.
plos-pone-0004311: In 2009, Fargallo, Martinez-Padilla, and Vinuela studied Spanish kestrels and their lunch. Kestrel-prey dynamics in a dry Mediterranean region hinged on generalist predators and climate. The dry southern system differed sharply from northern cycles. The neat study broadens predator-prey theory southward.
plos-pone-0351911: Cisplatin chemotherapy cures cancers but often destroys hearing as collateral damage. This study tested MnTBAP, an antioxidant compound, for its ability to protect the ear during cisplatin treatment. The otoprotective effect it found could let patients keep both their lives and their hearing.
plos-pone-0357411: Caring for someone with dementia demands a special kind of compassion — but what does that even mean? This paper published the protocol for a scoping review of how compassion is conceptualized in dementia caregiving. Mapping the concept first ensures the review captures what caregivers actually live.
plos-pone-0357011: We all judge evidence through ideological lenses — but by how much, exactly? This paper used a signal-detection approach to measure individual differences in ideologically biased evaluation of evidence. The method quantifies bias with precision, cleanly separating perceptual sensitivity from partisan slant.
plos-pone-0357311: Fake and adulterated agrochemicals cheat farmers out of harvests and money. This paper gathered farmers’, development agents’, and cooperative workers’ perspectives on the status, impacts, and solutions of agrochemical adulteration. The ground-level views point to fixes that might actually work where top-down rules have failed.
plos-pone-0351511: Anti-malarial drugs can damage the heart — and the mitochondria are the canary in the coal mine. This paper measured acute and prolonged effects of anti-malarials on mitochondrial respiration in atrial heart muscle cells for cardiac safety evaluation. The cellular data flag which drugs threaten the heart’s power supply before patients feel it.
plos-pone-0350111: Detecting ocean life from water samples depends heavily on how you filter. This study showed cost-efficient filtration and replication strategies match or exceed detection sensitivity for marine eDNA diversity at an intertidal site under a standardized protocol. The findings make eDNA biodiversity surveys both cheaper and more reliable.
plos-pone-0357811: Appendicitis severity varies enormously — and surgeons need reliable predictors before operating. This Palestinian retrospective cohort linked clinical, laboratory, operative, and appendiceal morphometric correlates to histopathological severity. The correlates help emergency teams triage cases with far greater confidence.
plos-pone-0357611: Fitspiration posts promise motivation but often deliver body pressure instead. This experimental study rethought fitspiration’s effects on young Chinese women, testing responses under controlled conditions. The experiments reveal the posts’ true psychological impact — inspiration or harm?
plos-pone-0356611: Treatment-resistant depression with elevated inflammation may yield to gentle brain stimulation. This paper tested the efficacy and safety of 15 mA transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) in these patients. The results offer cautious hope for a non-drug option where drugs have failed.
plos-pone-0348611: Clinical AI that hallucinates can kill — so safety constraints must be built in, not bolted on. CLIN-LLM is a safety-constrained hybrid framework for clinical diagnosis and treatment generation. The guardrailed architecture keeps AI’s clinical suggestions within safe, verifiable bounds.
plos-pone-0356811: Childhood tuberculosis in Rio de Janeiro rose and fell between 2010 and 2023 — but when did the turns happen? This Joinpoint analysis tracked temporal changes in pediatric TB incidence across those thirteen years. The identified trend breaks show exactly when control efforts worked — and when they failed.
plos-pone-0347811: Leaf litter teems with invertebrate life that traditional surveys miss. This paper assessed leaf-litter invertebrate biodiversity using high-throughput DNA sequencing. The molecular census reveals hidden diversity — and gives ecologists a faster way to monitor forest floor health.
plos-pone-0354711: Air pollution may be quietly damaging diabetics’ smallest blood vessels. This prospective cohort study examined the association between air pollution exposure and diabetic microvascular complications. The longitudinal design strengthens the case that dirty air accelerates the eye, kidney, and nerve damage of diabetes — adding urgency to clean-air policy.
plos-pone-0355711: Controlling nonlinear systems robustly — despite disturbances and uncertainty — is control theory’s holy grail. This paper developed observer-based optimal and robust output regulation for nonlinear systems. The mathematical advances bring guaranteed performance closer for real-world systems that refuse to behave linearly.
plos-pone-0355411: High-speed rail electrical cabinets run hot — and overheating components can halt trains. This paper built an LSTM-based temperature prediction model for key cabinet components. The predictive model enables maintenance before failure — keeping bullet trains running on schedule.
plos-pone-0355211: Network intrusions must be classified in real time — and reservoir computing offers speed. This paper applied reservoir computing to network intrusion classification. The brain-inspired approach processes network traffic with remarkable efficiency — promising faster cyber defenses.
plos-pone-0355611: Surgical instruments carry coded identities that AI must read in the operating room. This paper built a lightweight alignment-aware DBNet for surgical instrument code detection. The efficient detector reads instrument codes reliably amid the visual chaos of surgery — supporting automated safety checks.
plos-pone-0355111: Road cracks — the seeds of potholes — need automated detection at scale. This paper built an RPP-YOLOv11 model for road crack detection. The AI inspector promises cheaper, more comprehensive road surveys — catching cracks before they become craters.
plos-pone-0354511: Segmenting brain images in 3D — accurately and interpretably — remains AI’s challenge. TokenUNet makes a new case for transformer integration in efficient, interpretable 3D UNets for brain imaging. The architecture promises segmentations clinicians can both trust and understand.
europmc-pmc2846311: Learning a new word means linking sound to meaning, and this 2009 paper proposes the brain uses two cooperating systems. The authors present a complementary systems account of word learning backed by neural and behavioral evidence. Their model explains how fleeting encounters become lasting vocabulary. The theory shaped research on language acquisition.
europmc-pmc2852311: Blurry X-ray maps get honed by density fixes, and this 2010 paper tours the classic craft. The author sums fresh turns in classic density tweaks for shape work. The tour keeps tried math alive amid new fads. It stands as a field handbook.
europmc-pmc2881011: Medical students thrive with mentors, but programs vary wildly. This 2010 review surveys mentoring programs for medical students across the PubMed literature from 2000 to 2008. The authors distill what works, from pairing methods to meeting habits. Their review gave schools a blueprint for guiding young doctors.
europmc-pmc2891811: Spit in a tube at home and join science. This 2010 paper shows web-based, participant-driven studies can yield novel genetic associations for common traits. The authors validate the crowdsourced model. Their work launched direct-to-consumer genetics as a research force.
europmc-pmc2928211: Average trial results hide who truly gains. This 2010 paper urges trials to show how effects vary across patients, not just the mean. The authors give a plan for reporting the spread. Their push moved medicine toward personal proof. Readers can now ask who a drug helps most.
europmc-pmc2929211: Prostate cancer cells that shift shape gain stem-like powers. This 2010 paper ties the shape-shift, called EMT, to stem cell marks in prostate cancer cells. The authors link shape change to toughness. Their finding helps explain why these tumors resist treatment.
europmc-pmc2936111: Sea sponges host teeming bacterial partners passed between generations. This 2010 paper uses deep gene sequencing to reveal the diversity and handoff modes of sponge symbionts. The authors' dive exposes a hidden world of marine teamwork. Their work illuminates how sponges and germs live as one.
europmc-pmc2962811: Rare gene variants need special statistics, and this 2010 paper compares them. The authors evaluate statistical approaches to rare variant analysis in genetic association studies. Their bake-off guides gene hunters. The work shaped rare-variant methods. Its verdicts still steer study design today.
europmc-pmc2994911: Coughs spray flu virus into the air, and this 2010 paper measures how much. The authors trap influenza virus in aerosol bits from human coughs. Their counts show small particles carry the virus. The work shaped hospital air safety rules. Masks cut the airborne dose.
europmc-pmc3016411: Stem cells read how stiff their world feels. This 2011 paper shows stiffness gradients steer stem cell fate like real tissue does. The authors' finding guides tissue builders. Their work shaped regenerative medicine. Scaffolds now copy the body's stiffness map. Implant coatings now mimic the gradient.
europmc-pmc3020611: A flesh-eating staph went global. This 2003 paper tracks community MRSA carrying toxin genes as it spreads worldwide. The authors map the emergence. Their work warned hospitals everywhere. Healthy athletes and kids fell ill first. The toxin punches holes in white blood cells.
europmc-pmc3035611: Teen drinking casts long shadows. This 2011 review follows teen drinkers into adulthood across cohort studies. The authors tally addiction, job, and health costs. Their work informs alcohol policy. Early heavy drinking predicts adult dependence. Brain development takes the quietest hit.
europmc-pmc6535011: Forecasts of species doomed by climate change often ignore evolution - yet local adaptations can rescue populations. Studying bats, researchers showed that accounting for adaptive genetic variation sharply reduces projected range losses. The message for conservation: models that treat species as genetically uniform overstate extinction risk and may misdirect protection efforts.
europmc-pmc6544911: Checkpoint immunotherapy transforms some cancers but helps only a minority - picking the right patients is key. Tumors with broken DNA-repair (mismatch repair deficiency) or unstable genomes (MSI-high) respond far better to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 drugs. This review gathers the evidence behind the biomarker, which now guides who gets these powerful medicines.
europmc-pmc6554411: Type 2 diabetes unfolds when pancreatic beta cells - the body's insulin factories - falter. Using detailed metabolic tracing, researchers found diabetes sharply dials down the cells' mitochondrial engines, starving insulin release of energy. The work pins a key breakdown to the power plants themselves, sharpening the search for drugs that revive them.
europmc-pmc6660511: In Alzheimer's, the brain's immune cells - microglia - can turn harmful, and a protein called galectin-3 eggs them on. This study identifies galectin-3 as a previously unknown partner of TREM2, a key microglial receptor, driving damaging inflammation. Blocking the partnership could calm the brain's friendly fire.
europmc-pmc6696211: Each month, estrogen and progesterone choreograph the womb's lining - building it up, then shedding it. In endometriosis, the choreography fails: this review details what goes wrong in hormone signaling when uterine tissue grows where it should not. The missteps point to better treatments.
europmc-pmc6769011: CRISPR plus AAV delivery is gene therapy's dream team - with a hidden catch. This study found AAV vectors integrate into CRISPR-cut DNA at high rates, up to 47%. The unwanted insertions are a safety flag for therapies combining the two technologies.
gao-gaoreports-b-309911: A 2007 GAO ruling on a contract fight from the FitNet Purchasing Alliance, a frequent name in that year's protest docket. The group challenged how a federal buying pact was set up; the ruling parses the legal fine print. The call adds one more marker to the map of what agencies may and may not do when they buy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-11: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report examines the Office of Personnel Management — the federal government's HR agency — and finds opportunities to build on recent progress in its own workforce capacity. OPM advises agencies on hiring and talent, so GAO's review of its internal human-capital strength carried a certain symmetry. The report credits gains while pointing to unfinished work.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-711: American guns for Iraqi troops were vanishing into the fog in 2007 — GAO's report says the Pentagon could not prove U.S.-bought gear reached Iraqi forces. The findings describe an accountability black hole in the middle of a war. Weapons paid for by taxpayers, the report warns, were wandering without a paper trail.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-611: The thrift board wore many hats in 2007 — GAO's report maps the many duties Congress piled on the overseers of federal retirement investments. The findings inventory the sprawling mandate in plain terms. The report asks whether one board could sanely mind so many billions at once.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-411: The nation's emergency siren was aging in 2007 — GAO's report says the current alert system had limits, and the new integrated one needed building. The findings sound the warning. The report's plea: the alarm that warns America should actually reach America.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-211: Floating bases needed a real plan in 2007, and GAO's report says the joint seabasing concept wanted comprehensive management and rigorous testing. The findings demand the discipline. The report warns that the sea-base dream needed more than blueprints. The fleet had to prove it could float the idea.
openalex-w7207615311: Forty-three nursing students tried something new: quiz games on the Kahoot platform mixed with artificial intelligence tools in their coursework. The authors, their instructors, wrote up the experience to see whether game-style learning made the material stick better. This first-person account describes what they tried, how students responded, and what the experiment suggests about making nursing classes more interactive. Small and hands-on, it reads like a field note from the classroom.
openalex-w7204991111: Police forces face tangled rules and high pressure to perform. This paper proposes an integrated model that uses cognitive AI, systems meant to reason like analysts, to help the Parana military police govern better and stay operationally ready. The authors argue that smart systems can cut red tape while keeping legal safeguards. Ambitious and technical, it sketches a data-driven future for public security management.
openalex-w7204221811: Losing a pregnancy to miscarriage brings grief that nurses must meet with care. This paper reflects on empathy in nursing for women mourning a spontaneous abortion, drawing on Watson's theory of caring. The authors argue for nursing that honors the loss. Gentle and humane, it treats grief as clinical work.
openalex-w4411165211: Rare-earth metals hide their secrets in deep electron shells. This experimental paper mapped the valence electrons of all the 4f rare earths with hard X-ray photoemission. The authors used polarization to tease out the signals. A spectroscopy survey of the periodic table's most magnetic row.
openalex-w7155040111: Getting an ambulance to the right hospital fast is harder than it sounds. This study compared what made emergency transport difficult in Tokyo before and after COVID. The authors reviewed medical records across the pandemic divide. An emergency-medicine study of a system under strain.
openalex-w4415393411: Heatstroke cooks the body from within. This review covers the molecular mechanisms: how extreme heat triggers organ failure and cell death pathways. The authors mapped the pathophysiology. A medical review of heat as a killer, newly urgent in a warming world.
openalex-w7213942111: Surgery for long-term pancreas inflammation sometimes needs an encore. This how-to paper details pairing the Frey operation with tail removal when pain returns late. The authors laid out each key step. A surgery guide for a tough second operation on a scarred organ.
pmc-13437211: A 2026 review of imaging biomarkers for the glymphatic system — the brain's waste-clearance network — in the developing brain. Watching the plumbing work in children's brains requires specialized MRI techniques. The paper surveys which markers are ready and which need more work.
pmc-13420211: A 2026 study testing Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis CP-9 — a probiotic strain — on gut microbiota and immune function in healthy infants. Early-life microbes shape lifelong immunity, and the trial measured both. The findings inform which strains deserve a place in infant nutrition.
pmc-13343211: A 2026 scoping review of pelvic examination in undergraduate medical education — how it is taught, and how teaching is changing. The intimate exam is pedagogically and ethically sensitive. The review charts evolving best practice.
pmc-13486811: A 2026 hematology paper identifying IMP1 as a novel post-transcriptional regulator of early red blood cell development and embryonic globin output. The RNA-binding protein's role was previously unknown. The discovery adds a control layer to erythropoiesis.
pmc-13503111: A 2026 paper on novel protein biomarkers for risk stratification and personalized medicine. Proteins in blood can sort patients by risk. The biomarkers aim to personalize treatment decisions.
pmc-13444311: This 2026 psychiatry paper examined the relationship between childhood traumatic experiences and social anxiety disorders. Early trauma shapes adult social fear. The study quantifies the link.
pmc-13422811: A 2026 implementation evaluation protocol (DECIDE-T) for adopting a care pathway for children with medical complexity in pediatrics. Complex kids need coordinated pathways. The protocol structures the evaluation.
pmc-13630411: In this 2026 nanomedicine paper, a ferrous-supply-regenerating lipid nanoparticle integrating RNAi induced ferroptosis for cancer therapy. The particle fed iron to the death pathway. The combination is the strategy.
pmc-13619311: A 2026 AI paper introducing ProST — an image prompt-guided multimodal representation learning framework for spatial domain identification. Prompts guided the spatial learning. The framework is the contribution.
pmc-13530811: A 2026 conference poster on osteochondral allograft transplantation of the knee in "ideal" candidates — clinical outcomes and graft survivorship. The best-case results were documented. The poster sets the benchmark.
pmc-13530611: This 2026 conference poster addressed anatomic considerations for lateral extra-articular tenodesis in skeletally immature knees — avoiding the growth plate. The pediatric technique needed care. The poster guides it.
pmc-13448311: This 2026 conference abstract (BSLD-03) presented a pan-cancer atlas of leptomeningeal disease, revealing branched-chain keto acids driving immunosuppression and neurodegeneration. The metabolic culprits were identified. The atlas is the resource.
pmc-13544111: This 2026 One Health paper mapped spatial heterogeneity of Rift Valley fever burden in Kenya over 10 years using zDALY evaluation. The disease's geography was quantified. The evaluation guides control.
pmc-13531611: A 2026 sports medicine piece on sport-specific athletic adaptation. Different sports sculpt different athletes. The piece is the overview.
pmc-13501311: A 2026 software paper: Attracting Cavities 3.0 — faster, more versatile molecular docking for the SwissDock webserver. The docking upgrade is the deliverable. The speed is the selling point.
pmc-13470311: This 2026 case report and literature review covered pilon fracture with associated Achilles tendon rupture. The ankle fracture-tendon combination was reviewed. The case is the lesson.
pmc-13469911: This 2026 computer vision paper introduced a degradation-robust hue prior network for low-light rainy image restoration. The network saw through the gloom. The robustness is the advance.
pmc-13457511: This 2026 statistics paper presented network meta-analysis of survival outcomes with non-proportional hazards using flexible M-splines. The complex survival modeling was the advance. The splines handle the non-proportionality.
pmc-13439211: A 2026 wound care paper validating a YOLO-LabelMe hybrid AI model for automated assessment of pressure injury size and pocket. The AI measured the wounds. The validation is the evidence.

arxiv-2606-16011: Large language models sometimes change their answers when challenged — but how easily, and by whom? This paper tests whether models flip their answers under counterarguments, comparing pressure from the model itself versus pressure from a different model. It finds answer instability is real and measurable, which matters for anyone building AI systems that must stick to correct conclusions.
arxiv-2606-16111: AI agents that use tools — search engines, calculators, code runners — face tradeoffs: faster but less accurate, or slower but better. This paper trains such agents with Pareto-ranking policy optimization, aiming for agents that sit on the Pareto frontier: the best possible balance where no goal can improve without hurting another.
arxiv-2606-16211: Answering biomedical questions often requires hopping across several papers and databases. BioMedHop is a benchmark testing that multi-source reasoning, and BioWeave is a framework that weaves evidence from many sources together to answer. The paper gives the medical-AI community both a test and a method for evidence-grounded answers.
arxiv-2606-16311: In game theory, some games mix discrete choices (build or not) with continuous ones (how much). This paper asks when such mixed-integer games have "rational equilibria" — stable outcomes where every player's strategy is a clean, rational choice rather than a messy mix. The authors characterize the conditions, targeting game-theory and optimization researchers.
arxiv-2606-16511: Evaluating language models often comes down to the "tail" — rare failures and edge cases. This paper argues tail-shape estimation in LLM evaluation is fragile, prone to false alarms, and offers a protocol for diagnosing those false positives. It targets AI evaluators who want benchmarks that don't cry wolf.
arxiv-2606-16811: Teaching AI to reason usually needs tons of hand-labeled examples. This paper shows how to scale reasoning from minimal labels: a semi-supervised framework where a lightweight verifier checks the model's work. It is for AI researchers cutting labeling costs. Fewer labels, smarter checks.
